Main Case No.: C.C.No.1866 of 2023
 Proceeding Sheet
 Office

No
45. 31.03.2026 Dr, J

The present contempt case is filed for non-
 implementation of the orders dated 13.10.2022
 passed by this Court in W.P.No.12496 of 2022.
 The operative portion of the s

aid orders reads as  under:
 "Therefore, considering the submissions  made by both the counsel and considering the  averments made in the counter as well as the  reports of the Tahsildar, dated 04.02.2020 and  the Revenue Divisional Officer, dated  25.10.2021, the 2nd respondent-District Collector is directed to consider the reports of the Tahsildar, dated 04.02.2020 and the Revenue Divisional Officer, dated 25.10.2021, to issue clarification expeditiously as far as possible within a period of four (04) weeks, from the date of receipt of a copy of the order, to enable the respondents 3 and 4 to process the claims of the petitioners.

After receipt of such clarification from the 2nd respondent, the respondents 3 and 4 are directed to consider the claim of the petitioners and pay compensation as per G.O.Ms.No.259, dated 21.06.2016 and also as per the provisions of the Act,
2013 within a period of three (03) months."
(contd..)

After notice in the contempt case, the District Collector, who is happened to be the 1st respondent, has filed an affidavit in September, 2023 with the following averments:
"Further it is submitted that based on direction of this respondent, the District Survey and Land Records Officer, cancelled the Sy.Nos.292 to 298 and 299 to 304 allotted to the land which is being identified for alienation in favour of Enercon (India) Power Development Pvt Limited for setting up of windmills vide RC.
A1/986/2020 dated 06.02.2023.

Subsequently, the 3rd respondent herein who is Land Acquisition Officer, has initiated proceedings for the acquisition lands to an extent of 103.94 Acres in Sy Nos.292 to 305 of K.Bommepalli Village, Kondapuram and preliminary notification was also published on 30.06.2023 duly calling objections.

After completion of statutory period of 02 months from date of publication of P.N, the Land acquisition officer will pass award by following due The Operative Portion Of The Said Orders ... vs Unknown on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101775597/
1 procedure stipulated under law.

sentences.text: Subsequently, compensation amount will be paid to the petitioners.
Further it in submit that this respondent has no statutory role in present land acquisition proceedings and subsequent payment of compensation to the petitioners."
Subsequently, the 2nd contemnor has requested the 3rd contemnor for release of the amounts for payment of compensation to the petitioners based on award No.23 dated 14.12.2023.
After that, the respondents have (contd..) released the amounts only to the 16 petitioners and rest of the 18 petitioners the respondents have not released the amounts.

After notice, the other respondents have filed counters and subsequently, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.10 has submitted that they have filed review against the orders of this Court dated 13.10.2022.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners has placed reliance on the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Union of India v. Subedar Devassy PV ((2006) 1 SCC 613), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has considered the identical issue and made the following observations at paragraph Nos.2 and 6:
"2.

entities.text: Union of India v. Subedar Devassy PV ((2006) 1 SCC 613)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While dealing with an application for contempt, the court is really concerned with the question whether the earlier decision which has received its finality had been complied with or not.
It would not be permissible for a court to examine the correctness of the earlier decision which had not been assailed and to take a view different from what was taken in the earlier decision.
A similar view was taken in K.G. Derasari v. Union of India ([2001] 10 SCC 496).

entities.text: K.G. Derasari v. Union of India ([2001] 10 SCC 496)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The court exercising contempt jurisdiction is primarily concerned with the question of contumacious conduct of the party who is alleged to have committed default in complying with the directions in the judgment or order.
If there was no ambiguity or indefiniteness in the order, it is for the party concerned to approach the higher court if according to him the same is not legally (contd..) tenable.
Such a question has necessarily to be agitated before the higher court.
The court exercising contempt jurisdiction cannot take upon itself the power to decide the original proceedings in a manner not dealt with by the court passing the judgment or order.

Though strong reliance was placed by learned counsel for the appellants on a three-Judge Bench decision in Niaz Mohd. v. State of Haryana ([1994] 6 SCC 332),
we find that the same has no application to the facts of the present case.

entities.text: Niaz Mohd. v. State of Haryana ([1994] 6 SCC 332)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case the question arose about the impossibility to obey the order.
If that was the stand of the appellants, the least it could have done was to assail correctness of the judgment before the higher court.

6. If any party concerned is aggrieved by the order which in its opinion is wrong or against the rules or its implementation is neither practicable nor feasible, it should always either approach the court that passed the order or invoke jurisdiction of the appellate court.
Rightness or wrongness of the order cannot be urged in contempt proceedings.
Right or wrong, the order has to be obeyed.
Flouting an order of the court would render the party liable for contempt.
While dealing with an application for contempt, the court cannot traverse beyond the order, non- compliance with which is alleged.
In other words, it cannot say what should not have been done or what should have been done.
It cannot traverse beyond the order.
It cannot test correctness or otherwise of the order or give additional direction or delete any direction.
That would be exercising (contd..) review jurisdiction while dealing with an application for initiation of contempt proceedings.

The same The Operative Portion Of The Said Orders ... vs Unknown on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101775597/
2 would be impermissible and indefensible."
Further, the learned counsel has also placed reliance on the other judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has followed the above ruling.

Considering the submissions and on perusal of the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred judgment, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that the respondents have flouted the orders of this Court.
To give one more chance, list the matter on 22.04.2026 for implementation of the orders.
If respondent Nos.10 and 11 failed to implement the orders, they shall appear before this Court along with the records.
